scope: Apple GPU FAST trees only; all switches are opt-in and require both mode and vendor guards
validation: No compilation, verification, testing, linting, import, candidate execution or measurement performed

cards.title: RF histogram passes with 32 column slots
affected_estimators: DecisionTree and composite callers reaching ensemble Builder
cards.mechanism: N_BLKS_FOR_COLS becomes 32 instead of the Apple default 40. Existing workspace sizing, column-round progression and ragged final passes consume this single value; every sampled feature remains scored.
prerequisites: The histogram builder must be reached
limitations: This changes columns per pass, not features cooperatively processed inside one block
Inputs sampling at most 32 columns may see no scheduling change
Do not mix legacy RF column override defines into either arm
More column rounds may outweigh the smaller live workspace

cards.title: RF histogram work descriptors covering eight rows per lane
affected_estimators: DecisionTree and composite callers reaching ensemble Builder
cards.mechanism: HIST_ITEMS_PER_THREAD becomes eight, yielding 1024 rows per 128-lane histogram work descriptor instead of 512. Existing grid-stride histogram kernels and device workload construction retain all rows and fixed bin precision; partition mapping remains independent.
limitations: Fewer descriptors can reduce parallelism on small frontiers
Do not combine legacy histogram-items overrides
F01 plus F02 needs its own whole-fit comparison

cards.title: RF two small-histogram split cells per threadgroup
affected_estimators: DecisionTree and composite callers reaching ensemble Builder
cards.mechanism: FBS_WARP_CELLS becomes two instead of four. Each split cell still owns one SIMD group; launch Y extent and shared-memory allocation derive from the same value. Revised from the dormant host-staged small-node path to the small-histogram split scheduler actually used by the device loop.
prerequisites: The existing byte-capacity gate admits the SIMD-group split kernel
limitations: This schedules small histogram cells, not a new node-row threshold
Large histogram cells retain the existing general split kernel
More threadgroups may cost more than reduced shared memory saves
All tie, min-leaf and candidate-fold semantics remain in the existing routines

cards.title: RF partition scan at double cooperative width
affected_estimators: DecisionTree and composite callers reaching ensemble Builder
cards.mechanism: AFT_RF_SCAN_WIDTH_SCALE doubles the inclusive segmented scan's threadgroup width while preserving the original TPB inside partition ops, workload keys and copy-back kernels. NodeSplitScratch allocates aggregates and block heads for the new scan width. Both sampled-label and plain partition scan launchers use it.
limitations: The public builder changes scan width from 128 to 256; nonstandard direct template widths need later resource qualification
Count and copy-back launches keep their original geometry
Larger shared-memory scans may reduce occupancy
Stable partition tails, empty segments, labels and weights require later quality coverage

cards.title: RF sampled-label and weight gather with four row stripes per lane
affected_estimators: Composite callers using sampled-order forest labels
cards.mechanism: AFT_RF_GATHER_ROWS changes the existing gather kernel from one sampled row per lane to four block-strided row positions. The launch covers four times as many positions per block, reuses each sampled row index for its label and optional weight, and guards each stripe independently.
prerequisites: The sampled-order gather runs; the normal Apple forest path has LABELS_SAMPLED_ORDER enabled
limitations: This is label/weight row-copy tiling, not a new RNG sampler or feature-matrix copy
An explicitly enabled fused-bootstrap route may skip this gather; keep that prerequisite identical across arms
Bootstrap draws, sorted-row policy and OOB membership are unchanged by the candidate
Large prediction-only workloads are unaffected

cards.title: ExtraTrees 64-thread coupled frontier geometry
affected_estimators: ExtraTree and RandomTreesEmbedding callers reaching this builder
cards.mechanism: _device_tpb selects 64 lanes, two Apple SIMD groups, instead of 128. Scoring shared reductions and per-lane accumulator work shrink accordingly. Range, score, partition, workspace and workload maps retain their existing coupling through DEVICE_TPB, preserving full row coverage.
limitations: This necessarily changes other frontier passes alongside score geometry; it is not an isolated score-only claim
This is a distinct 64-lane arm, not the previously rejected Apple 256-lane experiment
Do not combine legacy ET_TPB override defines
Full classification criteria, regression, bootstrap and best-first paths require later qualification

cards.title: ExtraTrees partition tile twice the search row budget
affected_estimators: ExtraTree and RandomTreesEmbedding callers reaching this builder
cards.mechanism: PART_ROWS_PER_THREAD becomes twice SEARCH_ROWS_PER_THREAD. At baseline Apple geometry, count/scan/scatter/copy-back cover 4096 rows per workgroup instead of 2048 using the existing stable multi-row partition implementation. Existing separate work-map construction handles unequal search and partition tiles.
limitations: The unequal tiles can introduce work-map staging cost and regress whole fits
F06 changes the absolute row tile, so the combination is a distinct experiment
Existing flag caching remains conditioned on one row per thread
Do not combine legacy partition/search-row override defines

cards.title: ExtraTrees more concurrent trees under a 1 GiB row-plane budget
affected_estimators: RandomTreesEmbedding and composite forest callers reaching this trainer
cards.mechanism: FOREST_ROW_SLOT_CAP increases from 2^26 to 2^27 Int32 slots per plane. The two row/partition planes therefore have a combined 1 GiB budget. Existing grouping admits more complete trees and hence independent nodes into the merged frontier without changing each tree's RNG, candidate features or growth policy.
prerequisites: A forest large enough that the original row-slot budget limits concurrent trees
limitations: One-tree fits and forests already fitting one group can be unchanged
Caller-supplied row_slot_cap remains authoritative
Other workspace and per-tree buffers add to the stated row-plane budget
Peak memory and allocation failures must be included in later full-workload qualification
Best-first max_batch_size continues to bound the number of concurrent trees

cards.title: ExtraTrees tiled feature ranges with paired row-address staging
affected_estimators: ExtraTree and RandomTreesEmbedding callers using tiled ranges
cards.mechanism: node_feature_range_tiled_kernel stages two grid-strided row addresses per lane, then applies each feature descriptor to both rows before advancing. The existing feature count, code tile, key ordering, min/max and missing-count reductions remain intact. Applies to both float and uint16-code instantiations.
prerequisites: Existing tiled-range route and resident row-major representation admitted
limitations: Untiled range fallback is unchanged
Additional row-address registers may cost occupancy
This does not retry the previously slower 16/32-code feature tiles; accepted ET_CODE_TILE stays eight
Tail rows, constant features, signed zero, finite extremes and missing-value handling need later coverage

cards.title: Isolation forest 64-thread tree build
cards.mechanism: IF_BUILD_TPB changes the default build launch from 128 to 64. Existing sampling, min/max, stable partition and gather loops use actual n_threads; serial threshold/path arithmetic and seed mapping remain in the original routines. Shared allocation capacity remains IF_BUILD_TPB_MAX.
limitations: Explicit caller build_tpb still overrides the default
Shared scratch capacity is unchanged, so any gain comes from scheduling and active-lane work rather than a smaller allocation
Sampling large input populations may become slower with fewer lanes
All subsample and feature-sample settings require later quality qualification

cards.title: Isolation forest paired-row path traversal
cards.mechanism: AFT_IF_PATH_ROWS makes each traversal lane own two block-strided query rows. Both global and range traversal kernels reuse the tree offset/outer loop across two independent Float32 accumulators, preserving each row's tree order. Both corresponding launch grids divide by twice the thread count; shard accumulators retain their original continuation semantics.
prerequisites: Resident global or range traversal kernel reached
limitations: No fused sigmoid/pow, normalization or threshold change
Tiny queries may leave the second stripe inactive
Traversal divergence and extra accumulators may offset loop reuse
Pooled-model runtime support retains all pre-existing limitations; no new multi-device support is claimed

cards.title: Isolation forest flattened four-cell sampled gather
cards.mechanism: The existing sampled matrix is flattened across rows and features. Each build lane copies a four-Float32 tile, reusing its first sampled-row lookup for cells remaining in that row and reloading the exact row index when crossing a row boundary. Tiles stride by four times the block width. Original sampled feature indices and guarded tail cells are retained.
prerequisites: IF_FAST_ROWMAJOR enabled; do not set MOJOLEARN_IF_ROWMAJOR_OFF
limitations: This is explicit device copy tiling, not a claim that the compiler emits vector memory instructions
Row-boundary divisions can outweigh lookup reuse on very narrow rows
Column-major fallback retains its original gather
F10 changes the tile stride and therefore needs a combined experiment
No observations, feature samples or RNG draws are removed
